title: hollow-is-measured-a-proof-must-red-when-its-build-is-reverted
intention: Hollow is measured, not asserted: a tester verb reverts each file a ticket's build wrote to its pre-build version in a scratch worktree, runs the named proof there, and requires at least one tooth declared for that ticket to go red per file -- recording the result on the seal.
why: Law 8 says a proof a hollow build couldn't pass, and today that clause is read, never run: measured 2026-09-07, 'hollow' appears in the tester once, in a comment (cli.py:82), and in no seal record. The four false greens found the same day (three tickets on test_trouble_panel.py, one on test_codemother.py) passed every check the system has because every check asks 'did the proof pass?' and none asks 'would it have passed without the build?'. The lived symptom: a peer leans on a green that proves nothing, and finds out in production -- exactly the 'hollow green worse than a red' Law 8 names.
how: (a) `cairn test --hollow <ticket-id>`: read the ticket; resolve its decompose berth (chart_chain.decompose) and collect every sub_problem's writes_to under the cairn repo; read the BUILDME crossing's `at` from the ticket's owning journal (crossings carry at, proven_by, fingerprint; no commit) and take the pre-build commit as `git rev-list -1 --before=<at> HEAD`. (b) Create one scratch git worktree per run under the tester's scratch root (scratch.py), and for each writes_to file: check out the pre-build version there (`git show <commit>:<path>`), or remove it when it did not exist then; run the named proof in that worktree through run_proof (cwd = worktree, PYTHONPATH = worktree) with the instance swap the tester already uses; read evidence.teeth_green against PROVES[ticket] (tool cairn/tools/proof_coverage, ticket proof-coverage-is-declared-...); restore the file before the next. A file whose reversion reds no declared tooth is named: 'hollow: <file> reverted, no declared tooth redded' and the verb exits non-zero. (c) The result lands as evidence.hollow[ticket] = {file: [teeth that redded]} on the proof's seal record through persist_validation -- inside evidence, no ninth field; `--seal --hollow <ticket>` seals and measures in one run so the record is one write. (d) The worktree is removed at exit and on failure; the live tree is never touched (git status before == after, a tooth in the proof). The PROVEME->PROVED gate (ticket 1accdc1781aa) REQUIRES evidence.hollow[ticket] on the seal with no hollow file named, for every code-seam; absent evidence is a deterministic red exactly as an absent seal is (ruling 2026-08-10 clearance-is-mandatory; Akien 2026-09-07: 'Gates are supposed to be hard, deterministic, state changes'). There is no advisory mode. Depends on P1 (PROVES + teeth_green).
falsifier: DONE when: (1) a fixture ticket whose decompose berth lists one writes_to file and whose proof declares one tooth for it: with the file reverted the declared tooth reds and the verb reports {file: [tooth]}, exit 0; (2) a fixture whose proof stays green after the reversion is reported 'hollow: <file> reverted, no declared tooth redded', exit non-zero; (3) the live working tree is byte-identical before and after a run -- git status and a content hash of the writes_to files, measured in the proof; (4) the result lands as evidence.hollow[ticket] on the seal record and the record still carries exactly the ratified eight fields; (5) run against 9579a6f9cec6 once built, every writes_to file reds at least one declared tooth, recorded in that ticket's PROVEME crossing. WRONG INTENT if a full run on one ticket exceeds 5 minutes wall-clock on this box: then the per-file loop shares one worktree and one instance swap, not a different design.
traces_to: Law 8 -- verbatim: 'a proof a hollow build couldn't pass'; this is that clause as a verb. Law 3 -- nothing is known until measured; 'the proof exercises the build' was a hypothesis on every seal to date. Law 4 -- the rule becomes physics on the seal record. Law 9 -- a hollow green is worse than a red because a peer leans on it (Law 8's why: trust).
